findings.title: Unsafe dict access on integration.metadata['sender']['login'] can raise KeyError
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch(), the new user-validation check does `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` using direct dict indexing instead of `.get()`. The "sender" key in metadata is only ever set conditionally (via `state.get("sender")` in build_integration, or asynchronously by the webhook handler) and is not guaranteed to exist for every Integration row (e.g. legacy integrations created before this field existed, or installations where the webhook hasn't arrived/failed). If "sender" (or its "login" sub-key) is missing, this line raises an unhandled KeyError, producing a generic 500 error instead of the intended friendly 'Invalid installation request' page, defeating the purpose of this security-focused PR's graceful error handling.

findings.title: External GitHub API calls in OAuthLoginView are not exception-guarded
findings.body: `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` (line 423) and `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` (line 434) are called without try/except, unlike the subsequent response-parsing code which is wrapped in a broad `try/except Exception`. If GitHub's token endpoint or user endpoint fails due to network errors, timeouts, or returns an error status that causes the underlying client to raise (e.g. ApiError), the exception propagates unhandled, producing a generic 500 error instead of the intended 'Invalid installation request' error page that the rest of this view carefully produces for every other failure mode.

findings.title: Identity check relies on mutable GitHub username instead of immutable user ID
findings.body: `pipeline.bind_state("github_authenticated_user", authenticated_user_info["login"])` stores the GitHub "login" (username) which is mutable and can be renamed/reused by a different account over time. The later comparison in GitHubInstallation.dispatch (`!= integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`) also compares usernames rather than GitHub's immutable numeric user id. For a security-hardening change meant to prevent user-mismatch attacks, relying on a renamable/reusable identifier is weaker than comparing the stable account id that GitHub also provides in both the OAuth user info response and the webhook sender payload.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 'installation not found' code path
findings.body: The second request in `test_installation_not_found` now sends `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"`, which does not match the pipeline signature used everywhere else in this test file (`"9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"`). This causes the request to fail the new `OAuthLoginView` state-mismatch check (`request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature`) and return the generic 'Invalid installation request.' error before the code ever reaches `build_integration`'s GitHub-installation-404 handling that this test was originally written to verify. As a result, the originally intended scenario (GitHub API returning 404 when fetching installation info) is no longer actually covered by any test, even though the test name and the previous assertion ('The GitHub installation could not be found.') implied it was.

findings.title: No test for OAuth access_token exchange failure (invalid/reused code)
findings.body: The PR description explicitly calls out a third failure mode: 'If GitHub could not generate correct access_token from the code (wrong or attempt of re-use of code).' This path is implemented in OAuthLoginView (`if "access_token" not in payload: return error(...)`), but no test in this file simulates the `/login/oauth/access_token` endpoint returning a response without an access_token (e.g. an error/invalid_grant response) to confirm the pipeline correctly surfaces the failure page for this scenario.
